stem: What proportion of children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis continue to have active disease into adulthood?
explanation: Around 50% is the best estimate for persistence of active juvenile idiopathic arthritis into adulthood.
rationale: This question tests the key prognostic point that juvenile idiopathic arthritis often does not completely resolve by adulthood.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because roughly half of children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis continue to have active disease as adults.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the proportion persisting into adulthood is much higher than 10%.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because nearly all children do not continue with active disease into adulthood.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the persistence rate is not as high as 75%.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because about one quarter is too low an estimate for ongoing active disease into adulthood.

source.hint: It is essentially a coin flip whether the disease persists into their adult years.
